title: How many digits come after the point in a product?
description: One point six four times six and five point seven times thirteen point three five are written as fractions and multiplied. The digits after the point in each number are counted and matched to the zeros at the bottom. Keeko doubts that the second product is seven hundred and sixty point nine five.
teaching_notes: One idea: the digits after the point in a product are the digits after the point in the two numbers added together, because the zeros at the bottom of the fractions are multiplied. Watch for students who count the digits of only one number.

source: Find 1.64 × 6 and 5.7 × 13.35 as fractions, and count the digits after the decimal point in each number and in the product.
video_script.why: The child can write a decimal as a fraction and multiply, and now sees how the digits after the point in the product come from the two numbers.
video_script.substitution: the book's one point six four times six and five point seven times thirteen point three five
video_script.anchor: Two products from the book, one point six four times six and five point seven times thirteen point three five, with the digits after the point to be counted
video_script.wrong_answer: seven hundred and sixty point nine five
video_script.wrong_move: A common slip counts only the two digits after the point in thirteen point three five and leaves out the one digit in five point seven. The point is put after two places in seventy six thousand and ninety five, which gives seven hundred and sixty point nine five, far above the size check of about seventy eight.

final_answer.spoken: nine point eight four, and seventy six point zero nine five

maths_rules: digits after the point: 1.64 has 2, 6 has 0, 9.84 has 2 = 2 + 0
digits after the point: 5.7 has 1, 13.35 has 2, 76.095 has 3 = 1 + 2
size check: 1.5 × 6 = 9 and 1.64 is a little more than 1.5; 6 × 13 = 78, near 76.095
the slip: 76095 with two places is 760.95, counting only the places of 13.35
video_script.design: One idea: the zeros at the bottom of the two fractions multiply, so the digits after the point in the product are the digits after the point in the two numbers added. Assumes the writing of a decimal as a fraction. Wrong idea: counting the places of one number only. The two products stay all video; the decimals appear only on the answer beat.
